flows.period: week ending Wed Oct 21, 2026 (BofA/EPFR Flow Show, published Fri Oct 23)
flows.narrative: In the week ending Oct 21, emerging-market and China equity funds drew their strongest inflows in months even as BofA's institutional clients logged their 10th-largest weekly US equity selling week since 2008. Cash and Treasuries both gathered fresh money ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting, Europe booked a second straight week of outflows, and gold kept its safe-haven bid despite miners' rough October on the tape. Re-verified Monday 26 Oct pre-Asia-open: this remains the latest published BofA/EPFR edition -- the week-ended-Oct-28 edition is not due until early next week, so none of the figures below have moved. Newly incorporated this run: fuller detail on BofA's underlying client-flow book shows the headline institutional selling was accompanied by hedge funds turning net sellers (first time in 5 weeks) and retail/private clients also selling (reversing the prior 2 weeks' buying) -- a broader-based single-stock de-risking across all BofA client types than the institutional-only figure alone implies, even as fund-level (EPFR) flows stayed net positive.
